## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a Path tab (native path trace, native Linux and WSL2 only: on macOS, Windows and WSL1 `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row prefills it; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target field refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |

| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# DEVDESK-471 (P2-02) — Retirer l'onglet Path : le trace devient le sous-niveau de Diagnostics

Branche `feat/devdesk-471-remove-path-tab`, base `147593c0` (P2-01 / DEVDESK-470 mergé).
Sources lues : `internal/ui/netdiag/{model,update,view,header,trace_form,trace_level,path_model,path_view,path_from_route,path_source_flow}.go`,
les tests `path_*`, `trace_*`, `netdiag_path_tab_test.go`, `internal/app/{bar_attach,netdiag,netdiag_path_guard,activity_guard}_test.go`,
`internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go:289`, `docs/architecture/network.md` (l. 839-1093, 1300+), D144, D150, D152 (`docs/backlog.md`),
audit `.claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md` (checkout principal, option P2, tableau de correspondance l. 85-94).

## Questions bloquantes

1. **AC6, `esc` sur le formulaire prérempli depuis Status.** Aujourd'hui `OriginView` n'agit que sur les
   résultats (`handleKeyResults`) ; sur le formulaire (Status `H` sur un moniteur icmp/dns, sans auto-run),
   `esc` ne fait rien (`handleKeyInput`, `case "esc": return m, nil`). L'AC dit « `esc` revient à Status ».
   - (a) Ajouter : `esc` sur le formulaire, quand `OriginView != ""`, émet `BackToOriginMsg` (et le raccourci
     `esc Go back` apparaît dans le header du formulaire dans ce cas seulement).
   - (b) Ne rien changer : l'AC6 vise la non-régression du chemin résultats (auto-run) ; on ajoute seulement
     les tests de non-régression.
   - **Recommandation : (b)** : c'est le comportement actuel, la story ne retire que l'onglet Path, et (a) change une
     touche hors du périmètre de la story. Si l'utilisateur veut (a), c'est la seule sous-étape 4b, de taille S.
     Sans réponse, l'étape 4 applique (b).
2. **`enter` après un trace terminé, dans le sous-niveau.** D152 point 2 interdisait toute relance dans le
   sous-niveau. L'AC2 y fait déjà lancer le trace par `enter` (état prêt), et l'AC3 y rouvre `ctrl+o`.
   - (a) `enter` relance aussi après un trace terminé ou annulé (« Trace again »), comme l'onglet Path le
     faisait (`TestPathDoneEnterRelaunchesAndEscEdits`).
   - (b) `enter` ne lance que depuis l'état prêt ; pour relancer, il faut `esc`, puis `H` ou Trace Path.
   - **Recommandation : (a)** : l'AC7 demande de reprendre les comportements `path_*`, et l'ensemble de touches
     reste le même entre « prêt » et « terminé » (Rule 130). Sans réponse, le plan applique (a).

## Hypothèses (choix prudents, à valider par l'orchestrateur)

- H1. Choisir une source avec `ctrl+o` ne lance rien : le sous-niveau revient à l'état prêt, la cible est
  conservée et la colonne est vidée. Seul `enter` lance un trace (contrainte S-03b : rien ne part sans action explicite).
- H2. `H` est grisé, et refusé avec sa raison dans le footer, quand la cible des résultats ne peut pas être tracée
  (`parsePathTarget` la refuse, par exemple un littéral IPv6). Avant, l'onglet se préremplissait et c'est `enter` qui refusait.
  Ordre des raisons dans `pathFromRoute()` : plateforme, puis ligne de route, puis cible.
- H3. Les préfixes de log `ERROR [netdiag/path] …` ne changent pas. Ils nomment le moteur, pas une surface clavier,
  et 6 tests les vérifient.
- H4. Aucun fichier `path_*.go` n'est renommé : moins de conflits, `git blame` conservé, et les listes des gardes
  restent valides. Seuls quelques tests sont renommés quand leur nom ment (« Tab », « Field »).
- H5. Le sous-niveau ne montre ni la barre de filtre de Diagnostics ni aucune barre : footer de 3 lignes dans tous
  les états. Le footer propre au trace relève de P2-03.
- H6. Dans l'état prêt, le footer n'affiche aucun statut : le header dit `enter Trace the path` et `Target`.
  Le texte du footer du trace relève de P2-03.
- H7. La garde « un trace tourne déjà » de `H` et de Trace Path devient inatteignable : une fois l'onglet retiré,
  un trace en cours implique `StateTrace`, et `esc` annule avant de pouvoir sortir. La garde est gardée par défense,
  avec un seul texte `reasonPathBusy` (« A path trace is already running — esc cancels it »).
  `reasonTraceBusy`, qui cite « the Path tab », disparaît.

## Exigences non fonctionnelles

- Aucun paquet ne part sans `enter` explicite (S-03b, D144 point 4) : ni `H`, ni un changement de source ne lancent.
- Rule 110 : l'état change dans `Update` seulement ; `launch` garde ses Cmd purs (`startPathRun`).
- Rule 124 : footer de Diagnostics à 3 lignes dans le sous-niveau, quel que soit l'état. La hauteur déclarée est
  égale à la hauteur rendue.
- Rule 130 : `H`, `enter` et `ctrl+o` sont grisés avec la même raison que le refus ; l'ensemble des touches est le même
  en état prêt et en état terminé.
- `mise run test-race` : le générateur (`gen`) et l'annulation (`releaseRun`) ne changent pas, et le canal reste celui
  d'aujourd'hui.

## Options

| | A. Le sous-niveau pilote `pathModel`, qui perd son champ (retenue) | B. Garder `PathModel.input` caché comme porteur de la cible |
|---|---|---|
| Principe | Nouvel état `pathReady` (cible connue, rien envoyé), `ready(tg)` remplace `prefill`, le clavier du sous-niveau est explicite | Le champ invisible garde la cible ; `enter` le relit |
| Pour | Une seule saisie (R2 supprimé), plus de « champ caché » qui reprend le clavier (`handleDoneError`), `InEditMode` simple, et un code mort retiré | Diff plus petit dans `path_model.go` |
| Contre | Une vingtaine de tests au niveau `pm` à réécrire (le helper `launched` concentre l'essentiel) | Un état `pathEditing` inatteignable mais vivant, la garde `TestTraceLevelLettersDoNotReachTheHiddenField` à maintenir, `barView` mort, et `unused` à surveiller |

Option recommandée : **A**. Elle tient en 3 étapes livrables qui gardent la suite verte, l'onglet restant présent
pendant l'étape 1.

## Modèle cible

```
PathModel.state : pathReady (zéro, cible connue ou vide, rien envoyé) → pathRunning → pathDone (résultat ou errText)
Model.state     : StateInput / StateResults --(Trace Path | H)--> StateTrace ; traceOrigin = l'état d'où l'on vient
StateTrace      : esc (trace en cours) → annule → pathDone ; esc (sinon) → m.state = traceOrigin, sans rien réinitialiser
                  enter (prêt|terminé) → pm.launch(pm.target) ; ctrl+o → picker ; ↑↓ pgup pgdown home end → table
```

Interfaces (signatures finales, fin de l'étape 3) :

```go
// path_model.go
const ( pathReady pathState = iota; pathRunning; pathDone )
func (pm *PathModel) ready(tg pathTarget)                         // remplace prefill : state=pathReady, target=tg, source=hostSource(), picker=nil, clearRun()
func (pm *PathModel) launch(tg pathTarget) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) // inchangé + refuse silencieusement tg.Host == "" (défense)
func (pm *PathModel) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) // picker > ctrl+o > nav > running:esc > ready|done:enter
// trace_level.go
func (pm *PathModel) startFromForm(tg pathTarget) tea.Cmd         // ready(tg) puis launch(tg)
func (m *Model) openTrace(origin ViewState, tg pathTarget)        // m.traceOrigin=origin, m.state=StateTrace, pm.ready(tg)
func (m *Model) inTrace() bool                                    // m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.state == StateTrace
func (m *Model) handleKeyTrace(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd)
func (m *Model) escFromTrace() (*Model, tea.Cmd)                  // annule si en cours ; sinon retour à traceOrigin
func (m *Model) traceShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts               // seul constructeur des raccourcis du sous-niveau
// path_from_route.go
func (m *Model) pathFromRoute() shortcut.Availability             // traceable() → ligne Local route → parsePathTarget(host)
func (m *Model) tracePathFromRoute() (*Model, tea.Cmd)            // H : openTrace(StateResults, tg), aucun Cmd de trace
// model.go
traceOrigin ViewState // StateInput ou StateResults
```

Raccourcis du sous-niveau (`traceShortcuts`) :
- sélecteur ouvert (un mode, la liste est remplacée) : `enter Trace from it`, `esc Close` ;
- trace en cours (un mode) : `esc Cancel the trace` ;
- prêt et terminé (même ensemble de touches) : `tab Switch tab`, `enter Trace the path` en état prêt ou
  `Trace again` en état terminé (grisé si `!launchable`), `ctrl+o Trace from…` (grisé si `!sourceChoosable`),
  `esc Back to the results` ou `Back to the form` selon `traceOrigin`, `? Help`.

`1 → 2 → 3` en séquence (mêmes fichiers). `4a` après 2, en parallèle de 3. `4b` après 2 et seulement si Q1 = (a).
Une PR, fusionnée en squash : le commit unique sur `main` porte le code, les tests et les docs (AC7 : « même commit »).

## Risques

- R1 (moyen) : couplage du sélecteur et de `tab`. Un sélecteur ouvert doit garder `tab`, sinon on change d'onglet avec un
  sélecteur ouvert qui attend une liste. Couvert par `TestTraceLevelPickerHoldsTabAndEsc` et par `Init` (`closePicker`).
- R2 (moyen) : l'état gardé au retour (Rule 138). `resetToForm` ne doit pas être appelé, et le filtre et la sélection
  doivent survivre. Couvert par le test AC4 « résultats ».
- R3 (faible) : hauteur du footer (Rule 124). La barre de filtre de Diagnostics fuyait dans le sous-niveau
  (`GetFooterHeight` = `3 + ExtraHeight` en `StateTrace`). C'est un défaut latent de P2-01, corrigé à l'étape 1.
- R4 (faible) : à l'étape 1, l'onglet et le sous-niveau partagent `pm`. Un passage par l'onglet peut laisser `pm` en
  `pathEditing` puis revenir au sous-niveau ; `handleKeyTrace` est explicite (aucune lettre n'est transmise), donc il
  n'y a pas de fuite. L'état disparaît à l'étape 3.
- R5 (faible) : `bar_attach_test` (DEVDESK-457) utilisait la barre Path. L'intention est reprise sur deux autres barres,
  sans quoi la garde de jointure ne couvrirait plus le cas « corps rogné ».
- R6 (faible) : réécriture de l'aide. Les tests d'aide (`path_*_help_test.go`) vérifient des phrases précises. Garder
  ces phrases dans la section renommée.
- Points irréversibles : aucun. Pas de schéma de config, pas d'API publique, pas de fichier utilisateur. La décision
  produit (une seule saisie, plus d'onglet) est réversible par un revert.

## Brouillon d'entrée de backlog (pour `archivist`, pas d'ADR : local et réversible)

**D153 — DEVDESK-471 (P2-02) : l'onglet Path est retiré ; le trace n'existe plus que dans le sous-niveau de Diagnostics.**
Décidé : (1) La vue réseau a quatre onglets : Diagnostics, Ports, Interfaces, Forward. (2) `H` sur la ligne Local route
ouvre le sous-niveau (`StateTrace`) sur la cible des résultats, à l'état prêt, et ne lance jamais rien ; `enter` lance
(D144 point 4 conservé, son « onglet Path » remplacé). (3) Dans le sous-niveau, `enter` lance ou relance, `ctrl+o` ouvre
« Trace from » (exception déclarée, surface `netdiag/trace`, qui remplace `netdiag/path`), et `esc` annule le trace en
cours puis revient à l'écran d'origine (formulaire ou résultats) avec son état. Remplace le point 2 de D152 ; le coût
accepté au point 1 de D152 (champ de l'onglet écrasé) disparaît ; remplace le point 1 de D144. (4) `PathModel` n'a plus
de champ cible : la cible vient du formulaire, saisie une seule fois. (5) `H` est grisé, avec sa raison, sur une
plateforme qui ne trace pas et sur une cible que le trace refuse. (6) Changer de source revient à l'état prêt et ne lance
rien. Hypothèses : H1 à H7 du plan `.claude/plans/devdesk-471-remove-path-tab-plan.md`. **Plane :** DEVDESK-471.
Sources : ce plan, D144, D150 point 5, D152, l'audit `.claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md` (option P2).

20	const (
21		// defaultPathResolveTimeout bounds the name resolution of a target.
22		defaultPathResolveTimeout = 5 * time.Second
23	
24		// pathInputCharLimit holds a 253-character host name, a colon and a port.
25		pathInputCharLimit = 262
26	)
27	
28	// pathState is where the path trace is in its life cycle.
29	type pathState int
30	
31	const (
32		// pathEditing: the target field has the keyboard.
33		pathEditing pathState = iota
34		// pathRunning: a trace is in flight; the field is blurred.
35		pathRunning
36		// pathDone: a trace ended (or was canceled); the hops stay on screen.
37		pathDone
38		// pathReady: the target is known and nothing was sent; enter launches.
39		pathReady
40	)
41	
42	// PathModel is the path trace model: a target field above a table of hops that fills
43	// in while the trace runs.
44	type PathModel struct {
45		width  int
46		height int
47	
48		engine         pathEngine
49		resolveTimeout time.Duration
50	
51		input textinput.Model
52		table datatable.Model[pathStep]
53	
54		state  pathState
55		target pathTarget
56		addr   netip.Addr
57		// route is the way out of this machine; nil until the resolved message.
58		route *pathRoute
59		// hops is what the engine reported so far; the table shows
60		// visiblePathHops(hops). At done it is replaced by Result.Hops.
61		hops   []nettrace.Hop
62		result *nettrace.Result
63		// errText is the persistent footer error of a run that never traced. It is
64		// cleared by a change of the field or by the next launch, not by a timer.
65		errText string
66	
67		// gen identifies the run whose messages are accepted; cancel and msgs
68		// belong to that run.
69		gen    int
70		cancel context.CancelFunc
71		msgs   <-chan tea.Msg
72	
73		footer components.FooterMessage
74	
75		// source is where the trace starts: this machine, or a running container
76		// (DEVDESK-330). picker is the open selector, nil when closed; sourcesGen
77		// identifies the listing whose answer it accepts; container is what the
78		// column says about the source of the current run.
79		source     pathSource
80		picker     *pathSourcePicker
81		sourcesGen int
82		container  *pathContainer
83	
84		// platform is the WSL2 detection of the current run, set by handleResolved
85		// and cleared with the run.
86		platform wslenv.Info
87	}

89	// pathSourceKey opens the "Trace from" selector (declared exception, surface
90	// netdiag/trace).
91	const pathSourceKey = "ctrl+o"
92	
93	// pickerOpen reports whether the selector holds the keyboard.
94	func (pm *PathModel) pickerOpen() bool { return pm.picker != nil }
95	
96	func newPathModel(e pathEngine) *PathModel {
97		in := textinput.New()
98		theme.StyleTextInput(&in)
99		in.Placeholder = "hostname or IPv4 address"
100		in.CharLimit = pathInputCharLimit
101		in.Focus()
102	
103		return &PathModel{
104			engine:         e,
105			resolveTimeout: defaultPathResolveTimeout,
106			input:          in,
107			table: datatable.New(datatable.Config[pathStep]{
108				Columns:    pathColumns(),
109				SortColumn: -1, // the path order is the content
110			}),
111		}
112	}
113	
114	// InEditMode reports whether the target field has the keyboard.
115	// The open selector holds the keyboard too, from any state.
116	func (pm *PathModel) InEditMode() bool { return pm.state == pathEditing || pm.pickerOpen() }
117	
118	func (pm *PathModel) running() bool { return pm.state == pathRunning }
119	
120	func (pm *PathModel) resize(width, height int) {
121		pm.width = width
122		pm.height = max(height, 3)
123		pm.input.SetWidth(max(width-ansi.StringWidth(pathBarLabel)-4, 10))
124		pm.table.Resize(width, pm.height)
125	}
126	
127	// launchable is the one answer to "can a trace start here", read by the header
128	// and by the handler (Rule 130).
129	func (pm *PathModel) launchable() shortcut.Availability {
130		if err := pm.engine.supported(); err != nil {
131			return shortcut.Unavailable(pathUnsupportedReason(err))
132		}
133		return shortcut.Availability{}
134	}
135	
136	func (pm *PathModel) update(msg tea.Msg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
137		switch msg := msg.(type) {
138		case pathResolvedMsg:
139			return pm.handleResolved(msg)
140		case pathHopMsg:
141			return pm.handleHop(msg)
142		case pathDoneMsg:
143			return pm.handleDone(msg)
144		case pathSourcesMsg:
145			return pm.handleSources(msg)
146		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
147			return pm.handleKey(msg)
148		case tea.PasteMsg:
149			return pm.handlePaste(msg)
150		}
151		// Anything else is a footer expiry or the cursor blink of the field: the
152		// field needs the blink itself, or its cursor freezes.
153		pm.footer.Handle(msg)
154		var cmd tea.Cmd
155		pm.input, cmd = pm.input.Update(msg)
156		return pm, cmd
157	}
158	
159	func (pm *PathModel) handleResolved(msg pathResolvedMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
160		if msg.gen != pm.gen {
161			return pm, nil
162		}
163		pm.addr = msg.addr
164		pm.platform = msg.platform
165		route := newPathRoute(msg.route, msg.routeErr)
166		pm.route = &route
167		if !msg.source.isHost() {
168			c := newPathContainer(msg.source, msg.ctr, msg.ctrErr).withBridgeRead(msg.bridge)
169			pm.container = &c
170		}
171		pm.refreshSteps()
172		return pm, waitForPathMsg(pm.msgs)
173	}
174	
175	func (pm *PathModel) handleHop(msg pathHopMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
176		if msg.gen != pm.gen {
177			return pm, nil
178		}
179		pm.hops = append(pm.hops, msg.hop)
180		pm.refreshSteps()
181		return pm, waitForPathMsg(pm.msgs)
182	}
183	
184	func (pm *PathModel) handleDone(msg pathDoneMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
185		if msg.gen != pm.gen {
186			return pm, nil
187		}
188		pm.releaseRun()
189		if msg.err != nil {
190			return pm.handleDoneError(msg.err)
191		}
192		res := msg.result
193		pm.result = &res
194		pm.hops = res.Hops
195		pm.refreshSteps()
196		pm.state = pathDone
197		return pm, nil
198	}
199	
200	// handleDoneError ends a failed run. A kernel "no route" keeps the local rows
201	// (source, container, interface, gateway) with the route marked NoRoute; any
202	// other error clears every row.
203	func (pm *PathModel) handleDoneError(err error) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
204		pm.hops = nil
205		if nettrace.IsNoRoute(err) {
206			pm.route = &pathRoute{NoRoute: true}
207			pm.refreshSteps()
208		} else {
209			pm.route = nil
210			pm.container = nil
211			pm.platform = wslenv.Info{}
212			pm.table.SetItems(nil)
213		}
214		pm.errText = pathErrorLabel(pm.target.Host, err)
215		pm.state = pathDone
216		return pm, nil
217	}
218	
219	// refreshSteps rebuilds the table rows from the route and the hops.
220	func (pm *PathModel) refreshSteps() {
221		steps := withNoResponse(pathSteps(pm.container, pm.route, pm.hops), pm.result)
222		pm.table.SetItems(withWSL(steps, pm.platform))
223	}
224	
225	// clearRun forgets what the last run put on screen: the resolved address, the
226	// route, the container, the hops, the outcome and the error.
227	func (pm *PathModel) clearRun() {
228		pm.addr = netip.Addr{}
229		pm.hops = nil
230		pm.route = nil
231		pm.container = nil
232		pm.platform = wslenv.Info{}
233		pm.result = nil
234		pm.errText = ""
235		pm.table.SetItems(nil)
236	}
237	
238	// hopCount is the number of hop rows (the local rows are not counted).
239	func (pm *PathModel) hopCount() int {
240		n := 0
241		for _, s := range pm.table.Items() {
242			if s.Kind == stepHop {
243				n++
244			}
245		}
246		return n
247	}
248	
249	// releaseRun cancels the run's context (releasing it) and forgets its channel.
250	func (pm *PathModel) releaseRun() {
251		if pm.cancel != nil {
252			pm.cancel()
253			pm.cancel = nil
254		}
255		pm.msgs = nil
256	}
257	
258	func isPathNavKey(key string) bool {
259		switch key {
260		case "up", "down", "pgup", "pgdown", "home", "end":
261			return true
262		}
263		return false
264	}
265	
266	func (pm *PathModel) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
267		key := msg.String()
268		if pm.pickerOpen() {
269			return pm.handlePickerKey(key)
270		}
271		if key == pathSourceKey {
272			return pm.openPicker()
273		}
274		if isPathNavKey(key) {
275			return pm, pm.table.Update(msg)
276		}
277		switch pm.state {
278		case pathEditing:
279			return pm.handleEditKey(msg)
280		case pathRunning:
281			if key == "esc" {
282				return pm.cancelRun()
283			}
284		case pathDone, pathReady:
285			switch key {
286			case "enter":
287				return pm.launch(pm.target)
288			case "esc":
289				pm.state = pathEditing
290				return pm, pm.input.Focus()
291			}
292		}
293		return pm, nil
294	}
295	
296	func (pm *PathModel) handleEditKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
297		switch msg.String() {
298		case "enter":
299			return pm.launchFromInput()
300		case "esc", "tab", "shift+tab":
301			return pm, nil
302		}
303		return pm.updateInput(msg)
304	}
305	
306	func (pm *PathModel) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
307		if pm.state != pathEditing || pm.pickerOpen() {
308			return pm, nil // a paste reaches the focused field only (Rule 111)
309		}
310		return pm.updateInput(msg)
311	}
312	
313	// updateInput hands msg to the field; a changed value drops the stale error.
314	func (pm *PathModel) updateInput(msg tea.Msg) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
315		before := pm.input.Value()
316		var cmd tea.Cmd
317		pm.input, cmd = pm.input.Update(msg)
318		if pm.input.Value() != before {
319			pm.errText = ""
320		}
321		return pm, cmd
322	}
323	
324	func (pm *PathModel) launchFromInput() (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
325		tg, err := parsePathTarget(pm.input.Value())
326		if err != nil {
327			return pm, pm.footer.Error(capitalize(err.Error()))
328		}
329		return pm.launch(tg)
330	}
331	
332	// launch starts a run: the model changes here, in Update; the Cmd only does I/O.
333	func (pm *PathModel) launch(tg pathTarget) (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
334		if tg.Host == "" {
335			return pm, nil // nothing to trace
336		}
337		if a := pm.launchable(); !a.Enabled() {
338			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
339		}
340		pm.releaseRun()
341		pm.gen++
342		pm.target = tg
343		pm.clearRun()
344		pm.footer.Clear()
345	
346		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
347		ch := make(chan tea.Msg, pathChanCap)
348		pm.cancel, pm.msgs = cancel, ch
349		pm.input.Blur()
350		pm.state = pathRunning
351		return pm, startPathRun(ctx, pm.gen, tg, pm.source, pm.resolveTimeout, pm.engine, ch)
352	}
353	
354	// cancelRun answers esc at once: the run's late messages are dropped by the
355	// generation bump, the hops already seen stay on screen.
356	func (pm *PathModel) cancelRun() (*PathModel, tea.Cmd) {
357		pm.releaseRun()
358		pm.gen++
359		pm.result = &nettrace.Result{Outcome: nettrace.OutcomeCancelled}
360		pm.state = pathDone
361		return pm, nil
362	}
363	
364	// startPathRun builds the launch Cmd from values only, so that no closure
365	// reads the model (Rule 110).
366	func startPathRun(ctx context.Context, gen int, tg pathTarget, src pathSource, timeout time.Duration, e pathEngine, ch chan tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
367		return tea.Batch(
368			func() tea.Msg {
369				producePath(ctx, gen, tg, src, timeout, e, ch)
370				return nil
371			},
372			waitForPathMsg(ch),
373		)
374	}

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, native Linux and WSL2 only: on macOS, Windows and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci` (typed `StatusError`, `...Context` variants), `internal/imagesearch` and the registry browser's image search level, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/nettrace` (the path trace: unprivileged UDP + `IP_RECVERR`, Linux only) |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):

mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. **Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

# Go Patterns

> This file extends [common/patterns.md](../common/patterns.md) with Go specific content.

## Functional Options

```go
type Option func(*Server)

func WithPort(port int) Option {
    return func(s *Server) { s.port = port }
}

func NewServer(opts ...Option) *Server {
    s := &Server{port: 8080}
    for _, opt := range opts {
        opt(s)
    }
    return s
}
```

## Small Interfaces

Define interfaces where they are used, not where they are implemented.

## Dependency Injection

Use constructor functions to inject dependencies:

```go
func NewUserService(repo UserRepository, logger Logger) *UserService {
    return &UserService{repo: repo, logger: logger}
}
```

## Reference

See skill: `golang-patterns` for comprehensive Go patterns including concurrency, error handling, and package organization.

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Bordures étaient soustraites deux fois, ce qui tronquait la dernière colonne.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's
