## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.


## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Epics

There are no epic tools — an epic is a work item whose type is named "Epic". Work
items always belong to a project; ask which if one is not named.
1. type = `workitem_type resolve` with project_id and name="Epic" — type.id is the type_id.
2. Create: `workitem create` with project_id, type_id=type.id, name=...
3. List: `workitem list` with project_id and pql='type = "<type id>"'.
4. Read / update / delete / nest: `workitem retrieve` / `workitem update` /
   `workitem delete` by work item id (set parent=<work item id> to nest).
5. List an epic's children: `workitem list` with pql='childOf("<EPIC-IDENTIFIER>")'
   using the epic's human-readable identifier (e.g. "PROJ-12") from `workitem retrieve`.

1	package netdiag
2	
3	import (
4		"charm.land/bubbles/v2/textinput"
5		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
6		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/shortcut"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11	)
12	
13	const (
14		// traceTitleMargin is what the frame takes from the title line: corners,
15		// rules and the spaces around the title.
16		traceTitleMargin = 8
17	
18		// traceTitleTrail is what follows "Network" in the sub-level's title.
19		traceTitleTrail = " › Path › "
20	)
21	
22	// startFromForm starts a trace on tg from the Diagnostics form. It reuses this
23	// model rather than a second instance: the previous run is replaced, then the
24	// run is launched. It returns nil, and starts nothing, when the platform cannot
25	// trace. The Cmd does the I/O only (Rule 110).
26	func (pm *PathModel) startFromForm(tg pathTarget) tea.Cmd {
27		if !pm.launchable().Enabled() {
28			return nil
29		}
30		pm.ready(tg)
31		_, cmd := pm.launch(tg)
32		return cmd
33	}
34	
35	// ready puts the model in its ready state on tg: nothing is sent, the source is
36	// this machine and the previous run is forgotten.
37	func (pm *PathModel) ready(tg pathTarget) {
38		pm.state = pathReady
39		pm.target = tg
40		pm.source = hostSource()
41		pm.picker = nil
42		pm.clearRun()
43		pm.footer.Clear()
44		pm.input.SetValue(tg.Host)
45		pm.input.Blur()
46	}
47	
48	// openTrace enters the sub-level on tg, remembering where esc leads back to.
49	func (m *Model) openTrace(origin ViewState, tg pathTarget) {
50		m.traceOrigin = origin
51		m.state = StateTrace
52		m.activeTab = tabDiagnostics
53		m.pathModel.ready(tg)
54	}
55	
56	// inTrace reports whether the trace sub-level is on screen.
57	func (m *Model) inTrace() bool {
58		return m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.state == StateTrace
59	}
60	
61	// handleKeyTrace is the keyboard of the sub-level. It is explicit: esc, the
62	// table's navigation, ctrl+o and enter act (the last two only while no trace
63	// runs: the running mode lists esc alone), and every other key is dropped
64	// rather than handed to the Path model.
65	func (m *Model) handleKeyTrace(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
66		key := msg.String()
67		switch {
68		case key == "esc":
69			return m.escFromTrace()
70		case isPathNavKey(key):
71			return m, m.pathModel.table.Update(msg)
72		case key == pathSourceKey && !m.pathModel.running():
73			_, cmd := m.pathModel.openPicker()
74			return m, cmd
75		case key == "enter" && !m.pathModel.running():
76			_, cmd := m.pathModel.launch(m.pathModel.target)
77			return m, cmd
78		}
79		return m, nil
80	}
81	
82	// escFromTrace cancels a running trace; otherwise it goes back to where the
83	// sub-level was opened from, with its fields, focus, filter and results kept.
84	func (m *Model) escFromTrace() (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
85		if m.pathModel.running() {
86			_, cmd := m.pathModel.cancelRun()
87			return m, cmd
88		}
89		m.state = m.traceOrigin
90		if m.traceOrigin == StateInput {
91			m.restoreFormFocus()
92		}
93		return m, nil
94	}
95	
96	// restoreFormFocus puts the cursor back where focusedField says it is, so only
97	// that field blinks.
98	func (m *Model) restoreFormFocus() {
99		for _, in := range []*textinput.Model{&m.targetInput, &m.portInput, &m.dnsServerInput} {
100			in.Blur()
101		}
102		switch m.focusedField {
103		case fieldTarget:
104			m.targetInput.Focus()
105		case fieldPort:
106			m.portInput.Focus()
107		case fieldDNSServer:
108			m.dnsServerInput.Focus()
109		}
110	}
111	
112	// traceTitle is "Network › Path › host", the host cut with an ellipsis so the
113	// line never outgrows the frame.
114	func (m *Model) traceTitle(base string) string {
115		host := m.pathModel.target.Host
116		if m.width > 0 {
117			avail := m.width - traceTitleMargin - ansi.StringWidth(base+traceTitleTrail)
118			host = ansi.Truncate(host, max(avail, 1), "…")
119		}
120		return base + titleTrailStyle().Render(traceTitleTrail+host)
121	}
122	
123	// traceShortcuts is the only constructor of the sub-level's shortcuts. The
124	// selector and a running trace are modes and replace the list; ready and done
125	// share one key set, with greyed entries (Rule 130).
126	func (m *Model) traceShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
127		pm := m.pathModel
128		if pm.pickerOpen() {
129			return shortcut.Shortcuts{

75	// one (step 3 removes that case) it returns to editing.

108			m.dnsServerInput.Focus()
109		}

144		}

146			{Key: "tab", Description: "Switch tab"},
147			{Key: "enter", Description: enter, Disabled: !pm.launchable().Enabled()},
148			{Key: pathSourceKey, Description: "Trace from…", Disabled: !pm.sourceChoosable().Enabled()},
149			{Key: "esc", Description: esc},

70		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
71			m.width = msg.Width
72			m.height = msg.Height
73			m.resizeInputs()
74			m.filterBar.Resize(msg.Width)
75			m.rebuildChecksTable()
76			m.resizeDetailsViewport()
77			m.portsModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
78			m.interfacesModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
79			m.forwardModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
80			m.pathModel.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
81			return m, nil
82	
83		// The router's animation frame: the blink phase of the Ports dot and of the
84		// two footers that show the shared activity dot, whichever tab is on screen
85		// so a tab never comes back with a frozen phase.
86		case jobs.FrameMsg:
87			m.portsModel.table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
88			m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
89			m.interfacesModel.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
90			m.pathModel.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
91			return m, nil
92	
93		case stageDoneMsg:
94			return m.handleStageDone(msg)
95	
96		// Ports sub-model messages.
97		case portsTickMsg, portsDataMsg, portsKillResultMsg:
98			var cmd tea.Cmd
99			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
100			return m, cmd
101	
102		// The terminal focus reaches the ports poll on every tab: its tick runs
103		// whichever tab shows.
104		case shared.TerminalFocusMsg:
105			var cmd tea.Cmd
106			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
107			return m, cmd
108	
109		// Two tabs now ask before they act — Ports before a kill (§3.26), Forward
110		// before dropping the connections a redirection is carrying — so the answer
111		// goes to the tab that asked rather than to Ports unconditionally, which
112		// would have confirmed a kill from the Forward tab's modal.
113		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg, components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
114			return m.routeConfirm(msg)
115	
116		// Forward sub-model messages. ChangedMsg is the router's broadcast, and it
117		// reaches this view wherever it stands, on screen or not.
118		case forward.ChangedMsg, forwardTickMsg, ForwardFormSubmitMsg, ForwardFormCancelMsg:
119			var cmd tea.Cmd
120			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
121			return m, cmd
122	
123		// Path sub-model messages: a trace goes on, and its hops keep arriving,
124		// whichever tab is on screen.
125		case pathResolvedMsg, pathHopMsg, pathDoneMsg, pathSourcesMsg:
126			var cmd tea.Cmd
127			m.pathModel, cmd = m.pathModel.update(msg)
128			return m, cmd
129	
130		// Topology sub-model messages
131		case ifaceDataMsg:
132			var cmd tea.Cmd
133			m.interfacesModel, cmd = m.interfacesModel.update(msg)
134			return m, cmd
135	
136		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
137			return m.handleKey(msg)
138	
139		case tea.PasteMsg:
140			return m.handlePaste(msg)
141		}
142	
143		// Each tab holds its own footer, so an expiry has to be offered to all
144		// four, and the trace sub-level: the timer fires wherever the user has since
145		// navigated. The path model also takes the cursor blink of its field.
146		m.footer.Handle(msg)
147		m.portsModel.footer.Handle(msg)
148		m.interfacesModel.footer.Handle(msg)
149		m.forwardModel.footer.Handle(msg)
150		var cmd tea.Cmd
151		m.pathModel, cmd = m.pathModel.update(msg)
152		if m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.state == StateInput {
153			// The form's focused field owns the cursor blink.
154			var inputCmd tea.Cmd
155			m, inputCmd = m.updateActiveInput(msg)
156			cmd = tea.Batch(cmd, inputCmd)
157		}
158		return m, cmd
159	}
160	
161	// routeConfirm hands a confirmation answer to the tab that put the modal up.
162	func (m *Model) routeConfirm(msg tea.Msg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
163		var cmd tea.Cmd
164		if m.activeTab == tabForward {
165			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
166			return m, cmd
167		}
168		m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
169		return m, cmd
170	}
171	
172	// handleStageDone records one stage's answers and starts the next.
173	func (m *Model) handleStageDone(msg stageDoneMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
174		if msg.gen != m.runGen {
175			return m, nil // a superseded run
176		}
177		m.results = msg.results
178		m.rebuildChecksTable()
179	
180		steps := netcheck.Steps()
181		if msg.next >= len(steps) {
182			m.state = StateResults
183			m.verdict = netcheck.Summarize(m.results.All())
184			log.Printf("INFO [netdiag] run finished: verdict=%s over %d checks",
185				m.verdict, len(m.results.All()))
186			return m, nil
187		}
188	
189		m.runStep = msg.next
190		m.runStage = steps[msg.next]
191	
192		tg, err := m.buildTarget()
193		if err != nil {
194			// The form has not changed since the run started, so this cannot
195			// normally fail. Reporting it beats continuing with a target nobody
196			// can name.
197			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag] target became invalid mid-run: %v", err)
198			m.state = StateResults
199			return m, m.footer.Error("Run stopped — the target is no longer valid")
200		}
201		return m, runStageCmd(m.runGen, tg, m.checkSettings(), msg.next, m.results)
202	}
203	
204	// handlePaste gives pasted text to the field that has the keyboard on the tab on
205	// screen. It never reaches the key handlers, so no action fires (Rule 111).
206	func (m *Model) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
207		var cmd tea.Cmd
208		switch m.activeTab {
209		case tabPorts:
210			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
211		case tabInterfaces:
212			m.interfacesModel, cmd = m.interfacesModel.update(msg)
213		case tabForward:
214			m.forwardModel, cmd = m.forwardModel.update(msg)
215		default:
216			switch {
217			case m.filterBar.InEditMode():
218				m.filterBar, cmd = m.filterBar.Update(msg)
219				m.rebuildChecksTable()
220			case m.state == StateInput:
221				return m.updateActiveInput(msg)
222			}
223		}
224		return m, cmd
225	}
226	
227	func (m *Model) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
228		// A filter bar in edit mode claims every key before anything else, or a
229		// query cannot contain the letters the view binds.
230		if m.activeTab == tabDiagnostics && m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
231			var cmd tea.Cmd
232			m.filterBar, cmd = m.filterBar.Update(msg)
233			m.rebuildChecksTable()
234			return m, cmd
235		}
236	
237		// An open selector holds every key, tab included: it is a mode.
238		if m.inTrace() && m.pathModel.pickerOpen() {
239			var cmd tea.Cmd
240			m.pathModel, cmd = m.pathModel.update(msg)
241			return m, cmd
242		}
243	
244		// Tab / Shift+Tab cycles between the tabs (Rule 135)
245		switch msg.String() {
246		case "tab":
247			m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + 1) % tabCount
248			return m, nil
249		case "shift+tab":
250			m.activeTab = (m.activeTab + tabCount - 1) % tabCount
251			return m, nil
252		}
253	
254		// Route to active tab
255		if m.activeTab == tabPorts {
256			var cmd tea.Cmd
257			m.portsModel, cmd = m.portsModel.update(msg)
258			return m, cmd
259		}

12	// traceKeyTarget names the target field in the Trace Path validation.
13	const traceKeyTarget = "target"
14	
15	// traceable is the one answer to "can a trace start from the form", read by
16	// the button, the header and the handler (Rule 130).
17	func (m *Model) traceable() shortcut.Availability {
18		return m.pathModel.launchable()
19	}
20	
21	// traceTargetErrors is the validation of the target, with the path trace's own
22	// wording.
23	func (m *Model) traceTargetErrors() []components.FieldError {
24		if _, err := parsePathTarget(m.targetInput.Value()); err != nil {
25			return []components.FieldError{{Key: traceKeyTarget, Text: capitalize(err.Error())}}
26		}
27		return nil
28	}

30	// syncTraceMarks underlines the target only while it fails validation. Call it
31	// from Update() only (Rule 110).
32	func (m *Model) syncTraceMarks() {
33		m.traceMarks.Sync(traceKeyTarget, &m.targetInput, m.traceValidation.Invalid(traceKeyTarget))
34	}
35	
36	// revalidateTrace refreshes the target's error after an edit; it says nothing
37	// until a trace has been refused.
38	func (m *Model) revalidateTrace() {
39		m.traceValidation.Revalidate(m.traceTargetErrors())
40		m.syncTraceMarks()
41	}
42	
43	// traceFromForm handles enter on the Trace Path button. An unsupported
44	// platform is refused with its reason, a trace already running with a warning,
45	// an invalid target with an underline and a footer error; otherwise the trace
46	// sub-level opens on the Path model and the returned Cmd starts the run.
47	func (m *Model) traceFromForm() (*Model, tea.Cmd) {
48		if a := m.traceable(); !a.Enabled() {
49			return m, m.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
50		}
51		if m.pathModel.running() {
52			return m, m.footer.Warn(reasonPathBusy)
53		}
54		errs := m.traceTargetErrors()
55		m.traceValidation.Submit(errs)
56		m.syncTraceMarks()
57		if len(errs) > 0 {
58			return m, nil
59		}
60		tg, _ := parsePathTarget(m.targetInput.Value()) // accepted by traceTargetErrors
61		m.openTrace(StateInput, tg)
62		cmd := m.pathModel.startFromForm(tg)
63		// Posted after startFromForm: launching clears the sub-level's footer.
64		if n := traceUnusedNotice(m.portInput.Value(), m.dnsServerInput.Value()); n != "" {
65			cmd = tea.Batch(cmd, m.pathModel.footer.Info(n))
66		}
67		return m, cmd
68	}
69	
70	// traceUnusedNotice says which Diagnostics fields the path trace ignores: it
71	// probes the path to a host, so Port and DNS Server do not apply. Blank means
72	// not filled; it returns "" when neither is.
73	func traceUnusedNotice(port, dns string) string {
74		hasPort := strings.TrimSpace(port) != ""
75		hasDNS := strings.TrimSpace(dns) != ""
76		switch {
77		case hasPort && hasDNS:
78			return "Port and DNS Server are not used by the path trace"
79		case hasPort:
80			return "Port is not used by the path trace"
81		case hasDNS:
82			return "DNS Server is not used by the path trace"
83		}
84		return ""
85	}

content.content:
- the workspaces fuzzy finder (`internal/ui/fuzzy/finder.go`).
  DEVDESK-471): the hop-by-hop path to a target, from `internal/nettrace`
  (below). It was the fifth tab; it is now `StateTrace` of the Diagnostics tab
  (`tabCount = 4`), described under "The Trace Path button, `H` and the trace
  sub-level". It runs **no container**; since DEVDESK-330 it can name a running
  Docker Engine container as the source of the column (below), but the probes
  still leave from this machine. Three states: `pathReady` (target known,
  nothing sent), `pathRunning` (hops arriving) and `pathDone` (hops kept on
  screen). The **body is always the hop table** (`PathModel.view()` returns
  `table.View()`, Rule 139), in every state: columns Hop, Step, Address, RTT,
  with a silent hop dim and never red. **The column starts on this machine**
  (DEVDESK-329): three local rows, then the hops. `source` reads `this machine`;
  `interface` reads `<name> (<source address>)`; `gateway` reads the gateway
  address. The local rows have an empty Hop and RTT (they asked nobody; `-`
  means "no answer") and the default text colour. `pathSteps` (`path_steps.go`)
  is the only place that orders the rows; the table item is a `pathStep` (kind
  source, interface, gateway or hop; DEVDESK-330 adds container, network and
  trace, below).
  Nothing is shown before the route is known, so a resolution error leaves 0
  rows. There is **no target field**: the target is the Diagnostics form's (or
  the results' host for `H`), typed once. The sub-level's footer is 3 lines in
  every state (tab row, blank line, info line) and keeps its own
  `FooterMessage`, returned by `activeFooter`, so `WantsBlink()` follows a
  running trace. `Model.Running()` is true while a trace runs, so the router
  does not rebuild the view mid-trace.

  Keys: see "The Trace Path button, `H` and the trace sub-level" below (`enter`
  starts or traces again, `esc` cancels then goes back, `ctrl+o` opens *Trace
  neutral footer note, when: the engine is podman (`podman is not supported as a
  container source`, nothing invoked); `info` or `ps` fails, or no engine is
  present (`No Docker Engine reachable — only this machine is offered`; the raw
  error goes to the log as `ERROR [netdiag/path] sources: …`); the OS name
  starts with `Docker Desktop` (`Docker Desktop is not supported as a container
  source yet`, `ps` is not called); or no container runs (`No running container
  — only this machine is offered`). Docker Desktop is refused because its
  containers live in a VM: drawing their network before `this machine` would
  be false.
- **Choosing.** `enter` on the source already in use only closes the selector.
  Any other choice clears the column (rows, route, container, address, outcome,
  error), returns the tab to `pathEditing` with the field focused and its value
  kept, and shows a `Source` header field with the container name (absent for
  this machine). The column never mixes two sources. `H` from Diagnostics
  (`prefill`) resets the source to this machine: the route row it comes from is
  this machine's.
- **The container is read in the producer**, after the route lookup and before
  the trace (`inspectPathSource`, under the resolve timeout, killed by the run's
  context), and rides on `pathResolvedMsg` (`source`, `ctr`, `ctrErr`): no new
  message, capacity still 32. A trace from this machine never calls it. A
  failure is not fatal: the rows read `undetermined`, the trace runs, the raw
  A nil result changes nothing.
- **Nothing is concluded.** The rows say what was observed, never why: no cause
  and no "down". A silent hop most often means a router or firewall that does not
  answer these probes (ICMP filtering), which is a hypothesis; the rows do not
  state it.

**The target field takes no port (DEVDESK-335).** `parsePathTarget` accepts a
bare host name or IPv4 address. `host:80`, `[::1]:443` and `host:` are refused
with `Path ignores ports: enter a host or IP address only` (`errPathPort`,
footer level Error, nothing resolved, no trace). A literal IPv6 target stays
refused with the IPv6 error. `pathTarget` has no `Port` field. The probes are
UDP to port 33435 (`defaultProbePort`); the trace reaches a host, not a service.
This partly replaces point 3 of D144 (the port accepted and shown, not probed);
see D150 in `docs/backlog.md`. `traceroute_max_hops` is still not a
setting: the trace uses `nettrace.Options{}`.

  the results' host for `H`), typed once. The sub-level's footer is 3 lines in
  every state (tab row, blank line, info line) and keeps its own
  `FooterMessage`, returned by `activeFooter`, so `WantsBlink()` follows a
  running trace. `Model.Running()` is true while a trace runs, so the router
  does not rebuild the view mid-trace.

  Keys: see "The Trace Path button, `H` and the trace sub-level" below (`enter`
  starts or traces again, `esc` cancels then goes back, `ctrl+o` opens *Trace
  neutral footer note, when: the engine is podman (`podman is not supported as a
  container source`, nothing invoked); `info` or `ps` fails, or no engine is
  present (`No Docker Engine reachable — only this machine is offered`; the raw
  error goes to the log as `ERROR [netdiag/path] sources: …`); the OS name
  starts with `Docker Desktop` (`Docker Desktop is not supported as a container
  source yet`, `ps` is not called); or no container runs (`No running container
  — only this machine is offered`). Docker Desktop is refused because its
  containers live in a VM: drawing their network before `this machine` would
  be false.
- **Choosing.** `enter` on the source already in use only closes the selector.
  Any other choice clears the column (rows, route, container, address, outcome,
  error), returns the tab to `pathEditing` with the field focused and its value
  kept, and shows a `Source` header field with the container name (absent for
  this machine). The column never mixes two sources. `H` from Diagnostics
  (`prefill`) resets the source to this machine: the route row it comes from is
  this machine's.
- **The container is read in the producer**, after the route lookup and before
  the trace (`inspectPathSource`, under the resolve timeout, killed by the run's
  context), and rides on `pathResolvedMsg` (`source`, `ctr`, `ctrErr`): no new
  message, capacity still 32. A trace from this machine never calls it. A
  failure is not fatal: the rows read `undetermined`, the trace runs, the raw
  A nil result changes nothing.
- **Nothing is concluded.** The rows say what was observed, never why: no cause
  and no "down". A silent hop most often means a router or firewall that does not
  answer these probes (ICMP filtering), which is a hypothesis; the rows do not
  state it.

**The target field takes no port (DEVDESK-335).** `parsePathTarget` accepts a
bare host name or IPv4 address. `host:80`, `[::1]:443` and `host:` are refused
with `Path ignores ports: enter a host or IP address only` (`errPathPort`,
footer level Error, nothing resolved, no trace). A literal IPv6 target stays
refused with the IPv6 error. `pathTarget` has no `Port` field. The probes are
UDP to port 33435 (`defaultProbePort`); the trace reaches a host, not a service.
This partly replaces point 3 of D144 (the port accepted and shown, not probed);
see D150 in `docs/backlog.md`. `traceroute_max_hops` is still not a
setting: the trace uses `nettrace.Options{}`.

`handleDoneError` decides what stays on screen: when `nettrace.IsNoRoute(err)`

input.message:
Step 3 is done: `PathModel` no longer has a target field, and the 3 red tests in `path_model_no_field_test.go` pass without being weakened. Not committed.

Verification: `go build ./...` and `go vet` are clean. `golangci-lint run ./internal/ui/netdiag/... ./internal/ui/keymap/... ./internal/app/...` reports 0 issues. `gofmt -l` is clean and there are no CRs. `go test ./internal/ui/netdiag/... ./internal/ui/keymap/... -count=1` and `go test ./internal/app/ -run 'Bar|ActivityGuardScans|TestEscFromNetdiag|NetdiagOpen' -count=1` are green. I did not run `-race` or the full `./internal/app` suite.

**Production** (all under `internal/ui/netdiag/`)
- `path_model.go`:
  - Removed the textinput, `pathEditing`, `pathInputCharLimit`, `InEditMode`, `handleEditKey`, `handlePaste`, `updateInput`, `launchFromInput`, the paste branch of `update` and the `input.Blur`/`input.SetWidth` calls.
  - `pathReady` is now the zero value (ready, then running, then done).
  - `handleKey` order is: picker, `ctrl+o`, navigation, running (`esc` cancels, anything else ignored), then `enter` launches `pm.target`. `esc` outside a running trace does nothing, and `launch` already refuses an empty host.
  - `update` ends with `footer.Handle(msg)` and returns nil, so a paste is dropped.
- `path_view.go`: removed `pathBarLabel`, `barView` and `shortcuts()`; `traceShortcuts` is the only constructor.
- `path_from_route.go`: removed `prefill`.
- `path_source_flow.go`: `chooseSource` always goes back to `pathReady`, with the target kept and no focus.
- `trace_level.go`:
  - `ready` no longer touches an input.
  - `handleKeyTrace` is now: `esc` goes to `escFromTrace`; while a trace runs only navigation passes; everything else goes to `pm.handleKey`.
  - Behaviour is unchanged: `ctrl+o` while running is still silently ignored, with no footer warning.
- `update.go`: the final fallback is `m.pathModel.footer.Handle(msg)`, and the form input still takes the cursor blink.
- `path_run.go:28`: the comment no longer says "path tab".
- The «target field» wording is gone from the production code I touched. I found no help text to change in `path_model.go`; the one in `header.go` was already fine.

**Docs**
- `ui-components.md` (~l.731): the final `;` is now `.`.
- `network.md`:
  - Choosing a source goes back to `pathReady`, not `pathEditing` with the field focused.
  - `prefill` is replaced by `PathModel.ready`.
  - Added a paragraph saying `PathModel` has no target field and that `pathReady` is the zero value.
  - The key paragraph now describes the real `handleKeyTrace`.
  - The "target field takes no port" heading becomes "target takes no port".
  - Remaining "Path tab" mentions are historical.

**Tests**

Renamed or adapted, with the same coverage:
- `isTraceReady` is gone; every use is now `pm.state == pathReady` (or `!=`). That includes the red test file, where I only swapped the symbol.
- `launched(t, pm, target)` now calls `pm.ready(...)` then `enter`. It keeps the source a test chose, because several tests set `pm.source` first.
- New helper `pmShortcuts(pm)` wraps `traceShortcuts()`. It replaces the `pm.shortcuts()` calls in `path_model_test.go`, `path_platform_test.go` and `path_source_flow_test.go`.
- `TestPathNewModelIsAnEditableEmptyTable` became `TestPathNewModelIsAReadyEmptyTable`.
- `TestPathDoneEnterRelaunchesAndEscEdits` became `TestPathDoneEnterRelaunches`; its `esc`-edits part has no successor, because `esc` no longer edits.
- `TestTraceLevelLettersDoNotReachTheHiddenField` became `TestTraceLevelLettersAreInert`.
- `TestTraceLevelAFailedRunDoesNotLeakTheKeyboardToTheHiddenField` became `TestTraceLevelAFailedRunKeepsTheKeyboardInert`.
- `TestPathModelStartFromFormPrefillsThenLaunches` became `TestPathModelStartFromFormReadiesThenLaunches`.
- `TestPathPrefillDropsTheRoute` became `TestPathReadyDropsTheRoute`.
- `TestPathRelaunchAndPrefillResetTheContainer` became `TestPathRelaunchAndReadyResetTheContainer`.
- `TestTraceFormValidationTextMatchesThePathTab` became `TestTraceFormValidationTextMatchesTheTraceParser`.
- `TestPathSupportedPlatformHasNoStatusWhenEditing` became `...WhenReady`.
- `Type(...)` became `ready(...)` in `path_flow_test.go`, `path_noresponse_test.go` and `path_source_flow_test.go`; `InEditMode()` became a `state == pathDone` check in `path_column_test.go`, `path_column_layout_test.go` and `trace_level_standalone_test.go`.
- `path_from_route_test.go` now reads `target.Host` instead of the input.

Deleted, each with a successor:
- `TestPathBarShowsTheTargetFieldAndTheLaunchKeyIsListed` is replaced by the new `TestTraceLevelEnterLabelFollowsTheState` ("Trace the path" when ready, "Trace again" when done), plus the existing `TestTraceLevelShortcuts`.
- `TestPathShortcutsPerState` is covered by `TestTraceLevelShortcuts` and the `pmShortcuts` assertions.
- `TestPathRefusedPortIsNotATraceState` is now an assertion inside `TestTraceFormValidationRefusesAnInvalidTarget`, which checks the path model stays `pathReady` with no result, no error and no hops.
- `TestPathBareTargetsAreNotPortErrors` is now `TestTraceFormBareTargetsAreNotPortErrors`, with the same cases at form level.
- `TestPathLaunchRefusals` is covered by the form-level table, which I extended with `h:0` and `1.2.3.4:80`.
- `TestPathRunningIgnoresTypingAndPaste` and `TestPathPasteReachesTheFieldWhileEditing` are replaced by `TestPathIgnoresLettersAndPasteInEveryState` (ready, running, done).

The bar-height assertions in `TestPathBodyIsTheTableAndFooterHeightIsFixed` are removed, because `barView` no longer exists.
